script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

Title: THE LINEUP

INT. BASEBALL FIELD - DAY

A bustling baseball field. Fans in BLEACHERS cheer as PLAYERS jog to their positions on the GREEN GRASS. A crisp wind carries the scent of freshly cut grass and hot dogs.

INT. DUGOUT - DAY

Coach JIM (40s, stern but fair) gathers his TEAM.

COACH JIM
(passionately)
Gentlemen, we've got our shot. We're not the favorite to win, but we've got what it takes. Believe in yourselves and each other.

INT. LOCKER ROOM - DAY

During pre-game preparations. Players TONY (20s, cocky), JOSH (20s, insecure), and RAY (30s, veteran) share a moment.

TONY
(mocking)
Who needs "team spirit" when we've got talent?

JOSH
(nervously)
I don't know, man. We've lost the last three games...

RAY
(seriously)
The lineup matters, but so does how we work together. Remember that, kids.

INT. FIELD - DAY

First pitch thrown. The Game begins. Tense music plays.

INT. BATTER'S BOX - DAY

Josh faces the pitcher. He shakes, hesitates, then swings... and strikes out. He drops his bat, disappointed.

INT. DUGOUT - DAY

Coach Jim consoles Josh.

COACH JIM
(encouragingly)
Next time, you'll make it count.

INT. FIELD - DAY

Tony steps up to bat, confident. He strikes out, too. Frustration sets in.

INT. DUGOUT - DAY

Ray approaches Tony, concerned.

RAY
(calmly)
It's not just about you, kid. This team depends on each other.

INT. FIELD - DAY

Ray steps in for Tony, determined. He smashes a home run, sending the crowd into a frenzy.

INT. DUGOUT - DAY

Josh watches in awe. Confidence in his team builds.

INT. FIELD - DAY

The game continues. Tony regains his focus and hits a decisive homerun, cheers from the bench.

INT. FIELD - DAY

The game comes down to the final out. Ray faces the pitcher, everyone on edge. He strikes out, but the team celebrates as they've secured a win.

INT. LOCKER ROOM - NIGHT

Team members share stories of the game. A newfound sense of camaraderie.

TONY
(smiling)
I never realized it before, but you were right, Ray.

RAY
(grinning)
We all have our roles to play.

INT. FIELD - NIGHT

The sun sets on the baseball field, the team standing together in victory.

INT. DUGOUT - NIGHT

Coach Jim smiles, looking out at his team.

COACH JIM
(whispering)
The lineup matters, but teamwork is what truly makes a winner.

FADE OUT.
